argument: The Talent family is described twice as passive and permanently live [09-talents-abilities:13], [21-glossary:85], yet seven of the twenty-one talent cards are activated, limited-use cards: Fortune's Favor spends a Reaction [09-talents-abilities:27], Refuse to Fall a Reaction [:97], Miracle Worker a Reaction [:127], Battlefield Assessment a full Action [:177], Quick Study a Free action [:187], Chaotic Insight a Reaction [:197], and Rally the Troops a Maneuver [:207]. The glossary even names Fortune's Favor as its illustration of a talent while declaring the category activation-free, so the same word names two kinds of card. Term consistency also slips on usage limits: Renewal folds its per-scene limit into the Action field at [09-talents-abilities:529] where every other limited card states the limit in the body, and the same frequency phrase wanders between the front and back of a line within one card (Miracle Worker Novice [:129] versus Adept [:131]). Minimal fix: widen both definitions to say talents may be passive or limited-use activated cards, correct the glossary's example, and standardize the usage-limit phrase and its position in card bodies.

evidence.claim: Fortune's Favor occupies a Reaction, so this talent must be spent and cannot be permanently live as defined.

evidence.claim: Renewal alone hides its per-scene limit inside the Action header instead of stating it in the body as the other cards do.
Miracle Worker's Adept row leads with the frequency while its own Novice row trails with it, so limit placement drifts inside a single card.
